items.t: — Lucara Diamond sold 58,553 carats out of Karowe in the second quarter of 2026 against 77,167 a year earlier, and took $41.0 million against $43.7 million. Twenty-four per cent fewer stones for six per cent less money. Dividing the company's own revenue by its own carats gives $700.22 a carat realised against $566.30 a year ago, up 23.7%, arithmetic this desk has done and no source publishes. The company's own commentary runs the other way: tender prices down 5% and Clara prices down 17% on continued pressure in mid-range and lower-grade stones. Both are true, and the whole of the realisation gain is composition. It is not more big stones either, since specials above 10.8 carats came in at 176 against 242. Second-quarter net income was $15.6 million against $12.5 million, but first-half net income was $1.0 million against $12.4 million, which puts a loss of roughly $14.6 million in the first quarter by subtraction. Full-year guidance held at $100-130 million and 340,000-360,000 carats, leaving 201,703 to 221,703 carats to sell after halfway

— Kitco's live board at 05:59 New York time read gold $4,415.20 and silver $66.30, and the Editor wrote both back over caratwire's 04:59 marks of $4,401.70 and $66.03 under the one-price rule, with the timestamp and source named. Both were checked against TradingEconomics the same morning at $4,416.14 and $66.39, 0.02% and 0.14% away. Against this paper's own mark of record 24 hours earlier gold is up $42.40 or 0.97% and silver $1.51 or 2.33%. The gold-to-silver ratio, this desk's division of its own gold mark by its own silver mark, has now narrowed on four consecutive sessions: 68.41 on 9 August, 67.84 on 10 August, 67.49 on 11 August and 66.59 this morning. That is 1.82 points or 2.66% out of gold's purchasing power over silver in three sessions, and today's 0.90-point step is the largest of the four. Fine gold is $141.95 a gram

items.b: THE PLATINUM MARK THIS DESK WOULD NOT TAKE
items.t: — Platinum and palladium were not written back this morning, and the reason is printed on the page rather than buried. Kitco's platinum cell read $1,764.00, up $27.00 or 1.55%, which is the identical value and the identical change this paper printed yesterday. JM Bullion's board at 04:52 New York time bid $1,748.00. TradingEconomics read $1,761.30, up 0.36%. That is a span of $33.90 across three published pages inside an hour, or 1.94% of the metal, derived by this desk. Against that spread, and against a cell reproducing yesterday exactly, none of the three is a verified press-time reading, so caratwire's 04:59 mark of $1,747.00 stands as filed and is the figure JM Bullion's bid corroborates within a dollar. Palladium is handled identically: the tape carries $1,351.00 against $1,368.00 on Kitco and $1,392.59 on JM Bullion at 00:13, a 3.1% spread. An hour-old mark this paper can stand behind beats a fresh-looking one it cannot

items.b: ZALES GOES TO A TOY EXECUTIVE
items.t: — Signet Jewelers named Jamie Cygielman president of Zales and Banter on 11 August, starting 24 August, reporting directly to chief executive J.K. Symancyk and based in Dallas. She arrives from Mattel, where she was global head of dolls, a portfolio she reached after running American Girl as general manager and president and later widened to include Barbie. The same release named Pam Cloud president of Blue Nile with effect from 10 August, out of more than 25 years at Tiffany and Co., latterly senior vice president and chief merchandising officer, which this paper reported on 6 August. Two of Signet's four brand families changed president in eight days and the two hires are different in kind. Under Grow Brand Love, launched by Symancyk in March 2025, Signet runs four customer families: Kay and Peoples for core milestone and romantic gifting, Zales and Banter for style and trend, Jared for inspired luxury and Blue Nile for luxury. Luxury went to a merchant from inside the trade. Style and trend went to somebody who has never sold jewellery

items.b: A FLAT MONTH WITH A SHAPE INSIDE IT
items.t: — Rapaport's Diamond Pulse for August breaks open the flat July one-carat index this paper led on for 4 August. One-carat goods in D to F and G to J colour, in IF to VVS and VS clarity, averaged a gain of 0.1% in July. K to M colours averaged 1.7%. K to M in VS swung from a 0.1% loss to a 2.8% gain. The headline was flat because a near-flat top and a rising bottom cancelled inside it. The recovery this paper has described as bottom-up since 14 July now has a second dimension: it was already running from the bottom of the size chart, with 0.30-carat up 1.6% and 0.50-carat up 1.8% in the same month against a flat one-carat, and it is now also running from the bottom of the colour scale. One source, and it is the owner of the index reporting on its own index, with no second publisher of RapNet colour-band moves to check it against

— Two of the Bureau's six slate items were killed here on the archive test and both kills were available to the Bureau. The August Diamond Pulse's rough-production line, filed as unpublished after a string grep on 98.8 returned no hit, is in this paper's own archive: global rough production down 8% to 98.8 million carats in 2025 ran here on 27 July inside thirties-outrun-the-ones, with Russia leading by value for a third year. The Section 301 tariff bands in the same newsletter ran here on 25 July as tariff-wall-returns, at 10% and 12.5% effective 24 July, and the coloured-stone half of it ran on 23 July. Gem Diamonds' first-half figures, ranked second on the Bureau's slate and second on the marketing memo, were killed here yesterday as a repeat of 29 July and stay killed; this desk is not going to contradict its own published kill note two days later. The Shanghai gold contract at 947 yuan a gram could not be verified at source this morning and was not printed

— Colour has now missed eight consecutive editions, its last appearance being minus-point-one-for-color on 4 August, and it remains the longest dark streak on this paper's record. The Editor swept the beat independently rather than accepting the desk's file and returned only undated retailer trend copy: per-carat ruby averages with no publisher or method attached, and origin-report expansions dated to January. Nothing dated, sourced and unpublished exists in colour this morning. Gemfields' next mixed-quality auction is not until October and the Fancy Color Research Foundation was ruled out as a standing anchor yesterday because it puts its index behind membership. Watches is dark a third consecutive edition, with the Swiss federation's July export data not due until roughly 20 August and June's 11.2% already published here. Auctions is dark a third consecutive edition; Sotheby's Arcade Hong Kong result is still unpublished six days after close, and the Gem Drop sale in New York does not finish until 13 August

— The newest standards audit is caratcheck's file of 10 August and every item it listed under FOR CORRECTION TODAY was corrected in yesterday's run, on its own commit, ahead of the slate: the pull-quote element that set this paper's own analysis inside a quotation with a speech attribution was fixed at the renderer across all 235 article pages. No new standards file has been filed since. There is no outstanding correction on any published page this morning and no figure was altered today
